tasks.meervoude: Topic: Meervoude (plurals of nouns). Cover that a meervoud means more than one and that many nouns add -e (hond - honde, boek - boeke, huis - huise), some add -s (tafel - tafels, appel - appels), a short vowel doubles the consonant (kat - katte, kop - koppe), and kind has the special plural kinders. Ask for the plural of a given singular noun, which word is already plural, or which plural uses -s or -e. Use only nouns whose plural is certain and uniquely correct. Only use words, rules and examples consistent with this topic; do not test grammar from other topics. Write the question, all four options and the explanation in Afrikaans (Grade 6 First Additional Language), using correct standard Afrikaans spelling.
tasks.naamwoorde-lidwoorde: Topic: Naamwoorde en lidwoorde (nouns and the articles die and 'n). Cover that a selfstandige naamwoord is a naming word for a person, place, animal or thing (kat, boek, skool, hond, huis, water), that die means 'the' (specific noun, same for singular and plural), that 'n means 'a/an' (one non-specific thing, singular only), and that the article stands before the noun (die boek, 'n huis). Ask which word is a noun, which article fits, what 'n shows, or which phrase means 'the book' or 'a house'. Only use words, rules and examples consistent with this topic; do not test grammar from other topics. Write the question, all four options and the explanation in Afrikaans (Grade 6 First Additional Language), using correct standard Afrikaans spelling.
tasks.teenwoordige-tyd: Topic: Teenwoordige tyd (present tense). Cover that the present tense tells what happens now or usually (Ek speel = I play / I am playing), that the main verb (werkwoord, an action word) stays unchanged after Ek, Jy, Hy, Sy, Ons and Hulle with no -s added (Jy speel, Hy speel, Ons praat), and example verbs lees, skryf, drink, hardloop, praat, eet, loop, leer. Ask to pick the present-tense sentence, complete a sentence with the unchanged verb, or find the verb in a sentence. Distractors may use het ge-, sal or a wrong -s form. Only use words, rules and examples consistent with this topic; do not test grammar from other topics. Write the question, all four options and the explanation in Afrikaans (Grade 6 First Additional Language), using correct standard Afrikaans spelling.
tasks.woordeskat: Topic: Woordeskat en groete (everyday vocabulary and greetings). Cover the greetings Hallo (hello), Goeiemôre (good morning), Goeienaand (good evening), Totsiens (goodbye), the polite words Dankie (thank you) and Asseblief (please), and the common nouns kat (cat), hond (dog), huis (house), skool (school), boek (book) and water. Ask for the Afrikaans word for an English meaning or the English meaning of an Afrikaans word, and when a greeting is used. Spell Goeiemôre with the circumflex. Only use words, rules and examples consistent with this topic; do not test grammar from other topics. Write the question, all four options and the explanation in Afrikaans (Grade 6 First Additional Language), using correct standard Afrikaans spelling.
tasks.begripstoets: Topic: Begripstoets (reading comprehension). Cover reading a short, simple Afrikaans passage of two sentences (everyday topics such as school, sport, the garden, family, the weather) and answering one literal question from it: Waaroor gaan die teks (main idea, die hoofgedagte), finding facts (names, places, times, actions) by looking back in the text, and choosing die regte antwoord that matches the passage. Each question must contain the short passage followed by the question, and exactly one option must be stated in the passage. Only use words, rules and examples consistent with this topic; do not test grammar from other topics. Write the question, all four options and the explanation in Afrikaans (Grade 6 First Additional Language), using correct standard Afrikaans spelling.
tasks.byvoeglike-naamwoorde: Topic: Byvoeglike naamwoorde (adjectives). Cover that a byvoeglike naamwoord tells more about a noun (colour, size, quality), that in simple phrases it stands before the noun ('n mooi blom, 'n groot huis, 'n rooi appel, Die klein hond), and that some adjectives change form before a noun (goed - goeie, koud - koue, also vriendelike, nuwe, vinnige). Ask to pick the adjective in a phrase, choose the correct phrase or form, or say which word is a byvoeglike naamwoord. Only use words, rules and examples consistent with this topic; do not test grammar from other topics. Write the question, all four options and the explanation in Afrikaans (Grade 6 First Additional Language), using correct standard Afrikaans spelling.
tasks.verlede-tyd: Topic: Verlede tyd (past tense with het + ge-). Cover that the past tense uses het after the subject plus ge- on the verb (Ek loop - Ek het geloop; speel - gespeel, skop - geskop, lees - gelees, sien - gesien, werk - gewerk), eet becomes geëet, is becomes was (Ek was moeg), and het becomes het gehad (Hy het 'n pen gehad). In sentences with other words the ge- verb goes at the end (Ons het skool toe geloop). Ask to turn a present-tense sentence into the past tense. Make sure only one option is correct. Only use words, rules and examples consistent with this topic; do not test grammar from other topics. Write the question, all four options and the explanation in Afrikaans (Grade 6 First Additional Language), using correct standard Afrikaans spelling.
tasks.vriendskaplike-brief: Topic: Vriendskaplike brief (friendly letter). Cover the structure in order: datum (at the top, written day month year, for example 12 Mei 2024), groet (Liewe Sara, Liewe Ben), liggaam (the message: news, questions such as Hoe gaan dit met jou?, thanks, sentences such as Ek mis jou baie), afsluiting (a friendly ending such as Jou maatjie or Jou vriendin) and then the writer's naam. Formal forms (Geagte, Die uwe) do not belong in a friendly letter. Ask which part or line goes where, the correct order, or a suitable greeting or closing. Only use words, rules and examples consistent with this topic; do not test grammar from other topics. Write the question, all four options and the explanation in Afrikaans (Grade 6 First Additional Language), using correct standard Afrikaans spelling.
tasks.sinonieme-antonieme: Topic: Sinonieme en antonieme (synonyms and antonyms). Cover that sinonieme are words with the same or almost the same meaning (bly - gelukkig, vinnig - gou, praat - gesels, mooi - pragtig, kwaad - boos) and antonieme or teenoorgesteldes have opposite meanings (groot - klein, warm - koud, stadig - vinnig, lank - kort, oop - toe). Ask for a synonym or an antonym of a given word and read whether the question asks for same or opposite. Make sure only one option is correct. Only use words, rules and examples consistent with this topic; do not test grammar from other topics. Write the question, all four options and the explanation in Afrikaans (Grade 6 First Additional Language), using correct standard Afrikaans spelling.
tasks.sinsbou: Topic: Sinsbou (word order, STOMPI). Cover that in a normal Afrikaans statement the verb is in the second position (Ek speel buite, Ons eet vanaand pizza, Die hond slaap op die mat), that STOMPI orders ideas as subject, time, object, manner, place and infinitive (Ek lees vandag 'n boek), and that when a time phrase starts the sentence the verb stays second and the subject follows it (Vandag speel ek buite, Môre gaan ons skool toe, Na skool speel hulle sokker, Gister het ek huiswerk gedoen). Ask which sentence has the correct word order. Only use words, rules and examples consistent with this topic; do not test grammar from other topics. Write the question, all four options and the explanation in Afrikaans (Grade 6 First Additional Language), using correct standard Afrikaans spelling.
tasks.toekomende-tyd: Topic: Toekomende tyd (future tense with sal). Cover that the future tense uses sal before the action word, with the subject first and the main verb near the end of the sentence (Ek speel sokker - Ek sal sokker speel, Ons sal aandete eet, Hulle sal skool toe gaan, Die hond sal slaap). Ask to turn a present-tense statement into the future tense or which word shows the future (sal, not het, is or was). Wrong options may place sal after the verb, begin with Sal, or use het ge-. Only use words, rules and examples consistent with this topic; do not test grammar from other topics. Write the question, all four options and the explanation in Afrikaans (Grade 6 First Additional Language), using correct standard Afrikaans spelling.
tasks.trappe-van-vergelyking: Topic: Trappe van vergelyking (degrees of comparison: positive, comparative, superlative). Cover that Afrikaans compares in three steps, that many words add -er for more and -ste for most (mooi, mooier, mooiste; groot, groter, grootste; vinnig, vinniger, vinnigste; klein, kleiner; warm, warmer, warmste), and that goed is irregular (goed, beter, beste). Ask for the comparative or superlative of a given adjective. Distractors may use meer or mees, the wrong degree, or a regularised form such as goeder. Only use words, rules and examples consistent with this topic; do not test grammar from other topics. Write the question, all four options and the explanation in Afrikaans (Grade 6 First Additional Language), using correct standard Afrikaans spelling.
tasks.gemengde-hersiening: Topic: Gemengde hersiening (mixed revision). Cover vocabulary (venster - window), present tense (Hulle stap elke dag skool toe), past tense with het ge- (Gister het ek sokker gespeel, het geëet), future tense with sal (Môre sal ek my boek lees), plurals (boek - boeke), adjectives (vriendelik, rooi), synonyms (vinnig - gou) and prepositions (onder). Time words signal the tense: Vandag, Gister, Môre. Ask one fill-in-the-blank or choose-the-word question per item, each testing one of these skills with one clearly correct answer. Only use words, rules and examples consistent with this topic; do not test grammar from other topics. Write the question, all four options and the explanation in Afrikaans (Grade 6 First Additional Language), using correct standard Afrikaans spelling.
tasks.visuele-tekste: Topic: Visuele tekste (adverts, signs and posters). Cover reading short visual texts with key words, prices and instructions: vars (fresh), gratis (free), oop (open), moenie (do not), stilte (silence), gevaar (danger), and inference (what is advertised, who it is for, what to do; Net R10 means a low price). Examples: Vars brood net R10, Stilte asseblief, Koop 2 kry 1 gratis, Moenie ingaan nie, Gevaar: nat vloer, a school concert poster with day and time. Show the short text in the question and ask what is sold, what to do or what it means. Only use words, rules and examples consistent with this topic; do not test grammar from other topics. Write the question, all four options and the explanation in Afrikaans (Grade 6 First Additional Language), using correct standard Afrikaans spelling.
tasks.voegwoorde: Topic: Voegwoorde (conjunctions). Cover that voegwoorde join words, phrases or sentences: en (and), maar (but, contrast), want (because, gives a reason), of (or, a choice) and omdat (because, which often sends the verb to the end). Examples: Ek lees en ek skryf, Hy is klein, maar hy is sterk, Ek is moeg, want ek het hard gewerk, Wil jy appels of pere hê. Ask to fill a blank with the correct voegwoord from an English hint. Only one option may fit the meaning. Only use words, rules and examples consistent with this topic; do not test grammar from other topics. Write the question, all four options and the explanation in Afrikaans (Grade 6 First Additional Language), using correct standard Afrikaans spelling.
tasks.voorsetsels: Topic: Voorsetsels (prepositions of place). Cover that voorsetsels show where something is: op (on), in (in), onder (under), voor (in front of), agter (behind), langs (next to, beside), tussen (between) and by (at, by). Examples: Die boek lê op die tafel, Die hond slaap onder die bed, Die tuin is agter die skool, Ons wag by die hek. Ask to fill the blank with the Afrikaans voorsetsel that matches the English hint, so that only one option fits. Only use words, rules and examples consistent with this topic; do not test grammar from other topics. Write the question, all four options and the explanation in Afrikaans (Grade 6 First Additional Language), using correct standard Afrikaans spelling.
